description: Return a website, app, or agent to an earlier release. It publishes that release's files again as a new release, so the service gets the next version number, runs every release policy a publish runs, and keeps the history. Pass release, a version from list_releases, or omit it for the newest earlier release with different files. Repeating a call that names a release changes nothing; repeating one without release goes back another step. A release published before Valet kept its source cannot be restored. Environment variables, connectors, and access settings are not rolled back. Skills are refused: publish_skill publishes an earlier version. Requires connecting a Valet account.

idempotency_key.description: An opaque key of your choosing. Repeating a call with the same key returns the first call's result instead of rolling back a second time.

name.description: The website's, app's, or agent's name.

org_name.description: The Valet organization it belongs to. Omit to use the organization the account joined first.

release.description: The release version from list_releases to return to. Omit to return to the newest earlier release built from different files.

name: rollback_service

build_id.description: An app's rollback starts a build. Pass the ID to get_build and poll until deploy_state is up, idle, crashed, superseded, or refused. Absent for other kinds.

evaluation.description: The release evaluation. Without version, the release waits for its policies: follow it with get_evaluation. With version, the release is live and this is its monitor-only evaluation. Absent when the release has none.

deploy.description: What deploy did with the release: 'waiting' for the policies, 'live', or the code of the refusal. Absent when deploy has not decided.

deploy_message.description: The refusal's message when deploy refused the release, with credentials redacted as [redacted]. Absent otherwise.

id.description: ID of the release evaluation. Pass it to get_evaluation as evaluation_id.

monitor_findings.description: Count of findings monitor policies reported on a live release. They never block it; get_evaluation shows each. Absent when zero.

monitor_running.description: Names of monitor policies still pending or running on a live release. They never block it. Absent when none are.

redactions.description: How many credentials were replaced with [redacted] in the text this answer was built from: secret values the service holds, and strings shaped like an API key, a private key, a token, or a password in a URL or header. Redaction is best effort, so 0 does not prove the text holds no credential.

status.description: Status of the evaluation across its release policies. get_evaluation lists the per-policy results.

kind.description: Kind of the service: site, app, or agent.

name.description: Name of the website, app, or agent.

no_changes.description: True when the service already runs the release's files, so nothing was published. Absent otherwise.

org.description: Name of the Valet organization the call acted in.

pending.description: What the organization must set up before the agent deploys. Nothing was rolled back. Set each up with its tool, then call rollback_service again. Absent when the rollback went through.

attach.description: Connectors and channels the organization has but the agent does not hold, because publishing could not attach them: a Slack channel, which a person sets up, or one whose attach failed. Attach each to the agent.

catalog.description: The catalog entry the manifest names for it.

kind.description: Whether the dependency is a 'connector' or a 'channel'.

install.description: Connectors and channels the manifest names that the organization has no instance of. Create each from its catalog entry.

catalog.description: The catalog entry the manifest names for it.

kind.description: Whether the dependency is a 'connector' or a 'channel'.

skills.description: Skill references in the manifest that do not resolve.

restored.description: Version of the release whose files were restored. A repeat of a keyed call returns the same value.

url.description: URL that serves the website or app. Absent for an agent and while a site or app has no route.

version.description: Version number of the new release that went live. Absent when none did: the app builds first (see build_id), the release waits for its policies (see evaluation), or nothing changed.
